source_text:
4 {Gal 4,3} Ἐν τάξει τῶν ἐπιτρόπων καὶ οἰκονόμων τῶν τοὺς ἀτελεῖς τῇ
ἡλικίᾳ πρὸς τὸ συμφέρον παιδαγωγούντων ἔλαβε τὰ στοιχεῖα τοῦ κόσμου οἷς ἦμεν
διὰ τὸ τῆς γνώσεως ἀτελὲς συμφερόντως δεδουλωμένοι. οὐκ ἄν, ὡς οἶμαι, ἥλιον καὶ
σελήνην ἔλαβεν εἰς τάξιν τῶν ἐπιτρόπων διὰ τὸ ἀσύμφορον εἶναι τὴν εἰς ταῦτα
ὑποταγήν, ἀλλὰ στοιχεῖά φησι τοῦ κόσμου ἢ τὸν στοιχειώδη εἰσαγωγικὸν νόμον· καὶ
γὰρ τοῖς ἐξ Ἰουδαίων πιστοῖς ἔγραφεν, καὶ δηλοῖ τά τε μικρὸν ἀνωτέρω εἰρημένα καὶ
τὸ ἐὰν περιτέμνησθε Χριστὸς ὑμᾶς οὐδὲν ὠφελήσει.
thought_title: The elemental principles as guardians, not sun and moon
orientation: Gennadius is explaining Galatians 4:3, arguing that Paul's 'elemental principles of the world' are not the heavenly bodies but the introductory law given to the Jews.
pass_a_gloss: In the rank of guardians and stewards who tutor the immature in age toward what is beneficial, he took the elemental principles of the world, by which we were beneficially enslaved because of the incompleteness of knowledge. Paul would not, I think, have taken sun and moon into the rank of guardians, because subjection to these is improper, but he says elemental principles of the world, either the elementary introductory law; for indeed he was writing to the believers from the Jews, and both the things said a little above make this clear and the statement 'if you are circumcised, Christ will benefit you nothing.'

choices.term: Ἐν τάξει τῶν ἐπιτρόπων καὶ οἰκονόμων
choices.english: In the rank of guardians and stewards
choices.why: Keeps the military/orderly sense of τάξις as 'rank' and uses the fixed glossary terms for ἐπίτροποι and οἰκονόμοι.
rejected: In the position of guardians and stewards
In the role of guardians and stewards

choices.term: τῶν τοὺς ἀτελεῖς τῇ ἡλικίᾳ πρὸς τὸ συμφέρον παιδαγωγούντων
choices.english: who tutor the immature in age toward what is beneficial
choices.why: Preserves the participle's attributive force and the dative of respect τῇ ἡλικίᾳ, while using the glossary term 'tutors' as a verb.
rejected: who guide the young toward benefit
who discipline the underage for their good

choices.english: he took the elemental principles of the world
choices.why: Uses the fixed glossary rendering for στοιχεῖα τοῦ κόσμου and keeps the aorist 'took' to match Paul's act of writing.
rejected: he received the elemental principles of the world
he adopted the elemental principles of the world

choices.why: The adverb συμφερόντως modifies the participle δεδουλωμένοι, and 'beneficially' captures the sense of advantage or profit, echoing συμφέρον earlier.

choices.term: οὐκ ἄν, ὡς οἶμαι, ἥλιον καὶ σελήνην ἔλαβεν
choices.english: He would not, I think, have taken sun and moon
choices.why: The ἄν with aorist indicative expresses a counterfactual, and ὡς οἶμαι is a parenthetical hedge by Gennadius.
rejected: He did not, I think, take sun and moon
He would not have taken, I think, sun and moon

choices.why: Both adjectives modify νόμος; 'elementary' renders στοιχειώδη and 'introductory' renders εἰσαγωγικόν, keeping the pedagogical metaphor.

bible_refs.note: ἐὰν περιτέμνησθε Χριστὸς ὑμᾶς οὐδὲν ὠφελήσει

pass_b_english: Paul took the elemental principles of the world in the rank of guardians and stewards who tutor the immature in age toward what is beneficial—principles to which we were, because of our immature knowledge, beneficially enslaved (Galatians 4:3). He would not, I think, have taken sun and moon into the rank of guardians, because subjection to them would be unprofitable. Rather, by the elemental principles of the world he means either the elementary introductory law—for he was writing to believers from among the Jews, and both what he said a little earlier and the statement “if you are circumcised, Christ will benefit you nothing” (Galatians 5:2) make this clear.

last_rejected.source_quote: ἐὰν περιτέμνησθε Χριστὸς ὑμᾶς οὐδὲν ὠφελήσει
last_rejected.why: Source quotes Galatians 4:17 contextually; the citation Gal 5:2 is wrong verse.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐὰν περιτέμνησθε...οὐδὲν ὠφελήσει matches Gal 5:2 exactly, not 4:17. Citation is correct.

last_rejected.quote: Paul took the elemental principles of the world in the rank of guardians and stewards who tutor the immature in age toward what is beneficial
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἐν τάξει τῶν ἐπιτρόπων καὶ οἰκονόμων τῶν τοὺς ἀτελεῖς τῇ ἡλικίᾳ πρὸς τὸ συμφέρον παιδαγωγούντων ἔλαβε τὰ στοιχεῖα τοῦ κόσμου
last_rejected.why: Word order suggests 'He took the elemental principles in the rank of guardians...' i.e., he classified/treated them as guardians. 'Paul took...in the rank of' is unclear. 'ἔλαβε' here means 'took/understood/regarded as' not physically took. 'In the rank of' is awkward. Better: 'He understood the elemental principles in the class of guardians...'
last_rejected.ruling: ἔλαβε 'took' with ἐν τάξει 'in the rank of' is acceptable; meaning is not changed or lost.

last_rejected.why: Correct: 'believers from among the Jews' = 'the faithful from Jews'.
last_rejected.ruling: τοῖς ἐξ Ἰουδαίων πιστοῖς rendered correctly; checker confirms it. No error.

last_rejected.quote: what he said a little earlier
last_rejected.ruling: τά τε μικρὸν ἀνωτέρω εἰρημένα rendered correctly; checker confirms it. No error.
δηλοῖ rendered correctly; checker confirms it. No error.

problems.why: Same Greek concept (paidagogos/steward) rendered as guardians/stewards/tutors across sections; reader may miss they're synonyms for one role.
problems.fix: Use consistent term or note equivalence.

problems.quote: He would not, I think, have taken sun and moon into the rank of guardians
problems.why: 'He' refers to Paul, but after discussing 'elemental principles' as persons (guardians/stewards), reader may think 'he' means Eusebius or an opponent.

problems.quote: subjection to them would be unprofitable
problems.why: Gennadius argues against Eusebius's celestial reading; 'unprofitable' is weak—he means 'theologically wrong' or 'idolatrous', not merely 'not useful'.
Three related terms (guardians, stewards, tutors) used for same concept without clear distinction; reader may think different roles are meant.
problems.fix: Use one term consistently or explain they are synonyms for the same role.

problems.quote: principles to which we were, because of our immature knowledge, beneficially enslaved
problems.why: Comma-heavy and awkward; 'beneficially enslaved' is odd English that obscures meaning.
problems.fix: Rephrase: 'principles by which we were beneficially enslaved due to our immaturity.'

problems.why: 'Immature knowledge' is odd; likely means 'incomplete understanding' or spiritual immaturity, not knowledge that is itself immature.

edits.old: Paul took the elemental principles of the world in the rank of guardians and stewards who tutor the immature in age toward what is beneficial—principles to which we were, because of our immature knowledge, beneficially enslaved (Galatians 4:3).
edits.new: Paul took the elemental principles of the world in the rank of guardians and stewards who tutor the immature in age toward what is beneficial—principles by which we were beneficially enslaved because of our incomplete understanding (Galatians 4:3).

edits.old: He would not, I think, have taken sun and moon into the rank of guardians, because subjection to them would be unprofitable.
edits.new: Paul would not, I think, have taken sun and moon into the rank of guardians, because subjection to them would be improper.

fixed: The glossary problem about guardians/stewards/tutors is not a translation error; the source uses three distinct Greek terms (ἐπιτρόποι, οἰκονόμοι, παιδαγωγοί) and the English correctly renders each with its glossary-approved term. No change made.

The glossary problem about 'guardians and stewards' is not a translation error; the source uses two distinct Greek terms (ἐπιτρόποι, οἰκονόμοι) and the English correctly renders each with its glossary-approved term. No change made.
